theBigPicture: The US-Iran war is widening, with Houthi missiles striking airports in Saudi Arabia and Yemen and an attacked tanker forcing crew evacuations in the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most important oil shipping lane. Oil prices remain elevated with a war premium, even as US stocks hit an all-time high on optimism about artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, voters and politicians from Maine to Australia are pushing back on war costs and fossil fuel expansion.

householdImpact.energyAndFuel: Oil is still carrying a 'war premium' with Brent crude near $114 a barrel, so expect pump prices to stay high even after today's small dip. An explosion shut Venezuela's second-largest refinery, tightening global fuel supplies further.
householdImpact.borrowingAndMortgages: Financial markets are surprisingly calm right now, with low volatility and easy lending conditions, which is keeping mortgage, auto loan, and credit card rates steady for the moment. The risk is that a bigger escalation in the Middle East could jolt rates upward quickly.
householdImpact.groceriesAndSupplyChain: The attack on a tanker near the Strait of Hormuz threatens a shipping lane that carries a huge share of the world's oil, and Pakistan is already subsidizing fuel for 9 million people because war-driven energy costs are spilling into food and transport prices. Expect grocery bills to feel the squeeze as shipping and fuel costs climb.
householdImpact.jobsAndSavings: The stock market's record high is good news for 401(k)s and retirement accounts right now. But the rally leans heavily on a handful of big AI bets, so be prepared for bumps if war headlines worsen or investor mood turns.

globalFlashpoints.summary: Sweden is sending an air-defense missile system to Poland to guard the logistics hub that channels Western military aid into Ukraine.
Houthi missiles hit airports in Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Aden as the US-Iran war widens, and an attacked tanker in the Strait of Hormuz left 12 crew members injured.
Public anger is growing in Japan after a US Marine was arrested over the killing of a woman, putting strain on the American military presence there.

Nationwide protests are erupting in India over voter list changes, students are demonstrating at Cornell University, and power outages are hitting thousands of customers in Oregon and the Pacific Northwest.

topStories.headline: Houthi Missiles Strike Airports in Saudi Arabia and Yemen as War Widens
topStories.whyItMatters: The attacks on Saudi soil mark a dangerous expansion of the US-Iran conflict into one of the world's key oil regions. More strikes mean higher fuel prices and riskier shipping routes for everyday goods.

topStories.headline: Attacked Tanker in Strait of Hormuz: Oman Evacuates Injured Crew
topStories.whyItMatters: This narrow waterway carries a huge share of the world's oil, and attacks there directly push up what you pay at the pump. Eleven of the twelve injured crew members were Indian nationals.

topStories.headline: US Stock Market Hits All-Time High as Investors Bet Big on AI
topStories.whyItMatters: Your retirement account is likely enjoying the ride, but the record is built largely on artificial intelligence optimism. That makes markets more vulnerable to a sharp drop if war costs or debt worries spook investors.

topStories.headline: Trump's Suggestion That Iran Could 'Take' San Diego and Los Angeles Sparks Outrage From Both Parties
topStories.whyItMatters: Rare bipartisan backlash shows how politically risky the war has become at home, with even allies like Senator Susan Collins publicly opposing it. That growing split could shape upcoming elections and war funding decisions.

topStories.headline: Australian Court Blocks Coal Mine Expansion, Citing Climate Harm
topStories.whyItMatters: This landmark ruling forces companies to weigh climate damage before digging up more fossil fuels, setting a precedent that could ripple through energy projects and prices worldwide.

topStories.headline: Mali's Military Retakes Strategic Town of Kidal With Russian Backing
topStories.whyItMatters: Russia's growing military footprint in Africa is reshaping who holds power in resource-rich regions, which can affect global mining supplies and migration pressures.

topStories.headline: France's Presidential Candidates Face a Looming Financial Crisis
topStories.whyItMatters: Europe's second-largest economy is wrestling with debt troubles, and whatever promises candidates make could affect European markets, the value of the dollar, and prices Americans pay for imported goods.

whatWeAreWatching: Whether Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia pull the United States deeper into the war and send oil prices back up after today's dip.
Shipping traffic and insurance costs through the Strait of Hormuz, an early warning sign for future gas and grocery prices.
How French presidential candidates address the country's debt troubles, and whether markets get nervous about European finances.
US midterm projections now favoring Democrats for Senate control, and how the Iran war reshapes campaign messages.
The fallout from Venezuela's refinery explosion, which could tighten fuel supplies across the region.
The cluster of power outages in the Pacific Northwest and whether grid strain spreads as weather and infrastructure issues persist.
